text:
anya: heads up — I found ~120 sessions where the per-route token tally is lower than the client-side streaming count after reconnects. reproducer is a small app using streaming + toolcall. sample traces show router stitching chunks but billing missing tail tokens. anyone seen this? :thinking:

mike: is this mostly toolcall truncation or plain stream reconnects?

anya: mostly reconnects where client reconnects mid-stream and server resumes via resume_id. toolcall boundaries sometimes present too.

sam: can you paste a raw trace id?

anya: trace 01GXYZ sample below:
```
router: accept chunk A...
client: reconnect resume_id=abc123
router: stitch A -> B
runtime: emit tokens 120
billing: recorded tokens 80
```

mike: ok that's odd. could be router dropping tokens from the resume/tentative window.

julie: fyi we currently coalesce resume fragments and send a single session_resume event to billing. if billing's dedupe window runs before runtime commit we can lose the tail. propose adding a lightweight intent flag so ledger can decide.

sam: a header like `X-Resume-Intent: final|tentative` would help but worried about headers everywhere and perf. maybe emit a metric instead? :shrug:

anya: immediate ask: Console should surface raw per-chunk traces and mark tentative vs confirmed tokens — the current per-route graph hides ambiguity and makes debugging hard.

mike: agree on Console toggle. for telemetry we could add a `token_phase` label: `tentative`/`confirmed`/`toolcall` to keep cardinality small.

julie: implementation note — runtime already annotates chunks with `chunk_state: resume_candidate|committed`. router can map that to `token_phase` at ingest time without extra network headers. avoids perf hit.

sre-bot: alerting note — tentative tokens should not trigger hard quota enforcement. treat tentative as soft budget until confirmed.

sam: quick router pseudocode idea:
```
if resume_id and runtime.chunk_state == 'committed':
  token_phase = 'confirmed'
else:
  token_phase = 'tentative'
emit_to_billing(token_count, token_phase)
```

mike: what about toolcalls mid-stream? we used to attribute toolcall tokens to the model route instead of the tool route which confuses unit economics.

anya: exactly — when a toolcall happens mid-stream we should split attribution. either emit two ledger entries (model.tokens, tool.tokens) with same session_id/seq, or emit an attribution hint for postprocessing.

julie: ledger schema change is nontrivial. alternative: add `attrib_hint` metadata so the billing postprocessor can split without a full schema migration.

mike: UX question — how should Console visualize tentative vs confirmed? stacked bars with a hatch pattern for tentative would be clear.

anya: also add a small "Why tokens changed" link in route detail that expands sampled raw traces and highlights stitch points and reasons (reconnect|truncate|toolcall). that will speed oncall debugging.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: platform/router v2.12.5 -> canary

sam: canary the header-free approach (map runtime chunk_state->token_phase) to avoid touching ledger schema. roll to 5% and watch the tentative:confirmed ratio on affected routes.

julie: I'll open a tiny PR to wire token_phase into the ingest pipeline and add the Console toggle + an E2E to ensure quota logic excludes tentative tokens.

mike: also add a dashboard panel: `tentative token ratio` per route and alert if > 0.2 for 5m.

anya: thanks — I'll collect sample traces and paste them here for the canary. :thumbsup:
